q: A 10-year-old child presented with abdominal pain and vomiting. Lab values are given below. What is the next best step of management? Lab Values: RBS - 450 mg/dL pH - 7.0 HCO3 - 4 Na - 145 K - 4.8 meq/L (Q-30970202)
o: 10 ml/kg NS over 20 min (10% deficit correction) followed by insulin infusion with 20 mmol/L KCl
20 ml/kg 1/2 NS over 20 min (7% deficit correction) followed by insulin infusion and KCl 40 meq/L
20 ml/kg NS over 20 min with (10% deficit correction) followed by insulin infusion and KCl 40 meq/L
20 ml/kg RL over 20 min with (10% deficit correction) followed by insulin infusion and KCl 40 meq/L

q: A 29-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia has been stable on risperidone for the past few months. Recently, he began experiencing dystonia, for which he was started on benztropine 2 mg twice daily by his psychiatrist. A week later, he presents to the emergency department with complaints of dry mouth, blurred vision, confusion and urinary retention. On examination, he is disoriented, tachycardic, and febrile. Pupils are dilated and bowel sounds are absent. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient? (Q-84096521)
o: Discontinue risperidone and initiate lorazepam for possible neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS)
Administer intravenous dantrolene and initiate cooling measures for suspected serotonin syndrome
Start physostigmine with continuous cardiac monitoring for anticholinergic toxicity due to benztropine overdose
Administer activated charcoal and IV fluids; observe the patient as symptoms are likely self-limiting

q: An 18-year-old boy from Rajasthan weighing 50 kg is diagnosed with mixed P. vivax and P. falciparum malaria. What is the appropriate treatment regimen on day 2? (Q-44133064)
o: Artesunate 50 mg (4 tablets) + Primaquine 2.5 mg (6 tablets)
Artesunate 50 mg (4 tablets) + Primaquine 7.5 mg (6 tablets)
Artesunate 50 mg (4 tablets) + Sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine (750/37.5 mg) (2 tablets) + Primaquine 2.5 mg (6 tablets)
Artesunate 50 mg (4 tablets) + Sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine (750/37.5 mg) (2 tablets) + Primaquine 7.5 mg (6 tablets)

q: A 50 year old man presents with slow growing parotid mass for 8 months. The patient recently starts having difficulty closing the left eye. FNAC shows pleomorphic adenoma with atypia. Which of the following is the best treatment for this extent of tumor? (Q-73758920)
o: Superficial parotidectomy with resection of facial nerve and immediate cable grafting.
Total parotidectomy with resection of facial nerve and immediate cable grafting.
Radiotherapy done as there is no use of surgical intervention due to the widespread tumor extension.
Total conservation parotidectomy preserving the facial nerve as it may regenerate and become functional again after a few days of rest.
